description: Make a constitutive model(s) property assignment. Properties include density, bulk, shear, young, poisson, cohesion, friction, dilation, tension. Properties are name-value pairs where the name is the keyword given in the command and the value type is specific to the property. The assignment will affect any mpoint whose constitutive model includes the property named (noting that some properties, such as bulk, for instance, appear in many constitutive models) that is in range. All constitutive models have properties associated with them. The basic mechanical and option-specific mechanical constitutive models in MPoint are given below. All are classified as follows: elastic, elastic-plastic, dynamic, creep, thermal. Elastic Mechanical Models Anisotropic The anisotropic (transversely-elastic) model: properties, description. Elastic The isotropic elastic model: properties, description. Orthotropic The orthotropic elastic model: properties, description. Elastic-Plastic Mechanical Models Columnar-Basalt The columnar-basalt (COMBA) model: properties, description. Concrete The concrete model: properties, description. Cap-Yield The cap-yield (CYSoil) model: properties, description. Cap-Yield-Simplified The simplified Cap-Yield (CHSoil) model: properties, description. Double-Yield The double-yield model: properties, description. Drucker-Prager The Drucker-Prager model: properties, description. Hoek-Brown The Hoek-Brown model: properties, description. Hoek-Brown-PAC The Hoek-Brown-PAC model: properties, description. Modified-Cam-Clay The modified Cam-Clay model: properties, description. Mohr-Coulomb The Mohr-Coulomb model: properties, description. Mohr-Coulomb-Tension The Mohr-Coulomb tension (MorhT) model: properties, description. NorSand The NorSand model: properties, description. Plastic-Hardening The plastic hardening model: properties, description. Soft-Soil The soft-soil model: properties, description. Softening-Ubiquitous The bilinear strain-softening/hardening ubiquitous-joint model: properties, description. Strain-Softening The strain-softening/hardening Mohr-Coulomb model: properties, description. Swell The swell model: properties, description. Ubiquitous-Joint The ubiquitous-joint model: properties, description. Ubiquitous-Anisotropic The anisotropic-elasticity ubiquitous-joint model: properties, description. Von-Mises The von-mises model: properties, description. Dynamic Option Model Finn The Finn model: properties, description. P2PSand The P2PSand model: properties, description. IMASS Option Model IMASS The IMASS model: properties, description. Creep Option Models Burgers The Burgers model: properties, description. Burgers-Mohr The Burgers-Mohr model: properties, description. Columnar-Basalt The columnar-basalt (COMBA) model: properties, description. Maxwell The Maxwell (classic viscoplastic) model: properties, description. Power The power model: properties, description. Power-Mohr The power-Mohr model: properties, description. Power-Ubiquitous The power-ubiquitous model: properties, description. Soft-Soil-Creep The soft-soil-creep model: properties, description. WIPP The WIPP model: properties, description. WIPP-Drucker The WIPP-Drucker model: properties, description. WIPP-Salt The WIPP-salt model: properties, description. Thermal Option Model Hydration-Drucker-Prager The Hydration-Drucker-Prager model: properties, description.
notes: The 9.7 page for this command is a narrative catalogue of constitutive models, not a keyword table, so no keywords are parsed from it. The installed command index lists 'poisson', 'young' and one '{<model>}' group per model (43 in total).

The accepted property names depend on the constitutive model assigned by 'mpoint cmodel assign'. Use itasca_browse_reference(software='mpoint', topic='constitutive-models <model>') for the property vocabulary of a specific model.
